prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” dentist for implants in Denver — the right provider is the one with the right specialty, experience with the exact procedure you need, good outcomes, and a communication style you trust.

How to find the best provider for your implant
- Choose the right specialist for placement
  - Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS) — ideal for complex cases, extractions, bone grafting, and sedation.
  - Periodontists — specialists in gums and implants; excellent for single-tooth implants and grafting.
  - Prosthodontists — specialists in restoring teeth; great to design and place the final crown/bridge/arch.
  - Many teams combine an implant surgeon (OMS or periodontist) with a prosthodontist for the best result.
- Verify credentials and experience
  - Board certification (American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics) is a strong plus.
  - Years doing implants, number of implants placed, and experience with your specific case (e.g., immediate implant, full-arch, bone grafting, sinus lift).
- Ask to see before/after photos and patient references or reviews.
- Confirm they use modern diagnostics and technology
  - CBCT (3D) imaging, digital planning, guided surgery, and CAD/CAM restorations improve predictability.
- Get a written treatment plan and cost breakdown
  - Ask about success rates, possible complications, warranty/guarantee, and what happens if an implant fails.
- Check practical matters
  - Office location, after-hours care, sedation options, payment plans, and whether they coordinate with your restorative dentist.

Where to search and verify providers
- AAOMS (find an oral surgeon), AAID (implant dentists), American Academy of Periodontology — online “find a specialist” tools.
- Local resources: university dental clinics (University of Colorado School of Dental Medicine), Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Google and Yelp reviews.
- Insurance and financing: call your insurer and ask about covered providers; many practices offer financing.

Typical timeline and cost (Denver / US ranges)
- Timeline: 3–9+ months depending on extraction, grafting, healing, and restoration steps. Some “same-day” immediate-load options exist for properly selected patients.
- Cost: commonly $3,000–$6,000+ per tooth for implant + abutment + crown in the U.S.; costs vary with complexity and materials.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow options if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood in Denver.
- Provide a list of questions to bring to a consultation.
- Explain differences between one-stage vs two-stage implants, bone grafting, or “All-on-4” full-arch options.
